title: Canonical Quantum Gravity and the Problem of Time
version: arXiv gr-qc/9210011v1 (1992-10-21, only version); lectures, NATO ASI Salamanca June 1992; also published in Integrable Systems, Quantum Groups, and Quantum Field Studies vol. (per Earman 2003 reference list)
locator: Abstract; §1 preamble; §2.3 'Approaches to the Problem of Time' (categories I/II/III)
assumptions: Canonical (Hamiltonian) formulation of GR; Dirac-style constraint quantization as baseline
conclusion: All schemes divide into: (I) internal time identified and constraints solved before quantization; (II) constraints imposed at quantum level (Wheeler-DeWitt), time identified after; (III) schemes with no fundamental time
dependencies: Kuchar's companion review (his ref '?'), canonical decomposition of GR
relevance: The canonical 'Isham classification' named in the task; supplies the three-category scheme used in READING.md parts 1-2
limits: Fetched via ar5iv with windows read around the classification; formal/technical sections (canonical decomposition, each individual scheme) skimmed, not read line by line
open_questions: Whether category boundaries survive loop/shape-dynamics reformulations

title: On the Emergence of Time in Quantum Gravity
authors: J. Butterfield and C. J. Isham
version: arXiv gr-qc/9901024v1, 8 January 1999; PhilSci-Archive p1914
locator: §5.2.2 'What then is the problem of time?' (Kuchar's three forms); §5.4 WKB/semiclassical emergence and its problems; §4.1 fixity senses; §4.2 Barbour Machian summary
assumptions: Geometrodynamics as the home of the problem (following Kuchar); standard quantum theory
conclusion: The problem of time is a cluster from time being fixed in quantum theory (classical, nondynamical, same in all models) but not so in GR; semiclassical emergence of time is state-dependent, tied to WKB ansatz, and superposed WKB sectors carry separate times
proof_status: n/a (conceptual; WKB expansion reported, not proved)
relevance: Primary source for the philosophical treatment named in the task; supplies Kuchar's three forms and the emergence problems
limits: Fetched in full (150k chars); read in targeted windows (problem statement, Barbour summary, WKB conclusions); Euclidean-programme sections skimmed
open_questions: How one semiclassical sector is selected; loss of Schrodinger form at next WKB order

title: Forget time
version: arXiv 0903.3832v3, 27 March 2009 (ar5iv render of v3); essay for FQXi 'The Nature of Time' contest, dated August 2008
